discovery: Discovery of the cosmic infrared background

nominees.name: Jean-Loup Puget
nominees.affiliation: Institut d'Astrophysique Spatiale, Université Paris-Saclay, France

nominees.name: Michael G. Hauser
nominees.affiliation: Space Telescope Science Institute and NASA Goddard Space Flight Center (emeritus), USA

motivation: Puget and Hauser discovered the cosmic infrared background, the integrated glow of all dust-enshrouded star formation and accretion across cosmic history. Puget and collaborators first detected it in COBE/FIRAS data in 1996. Hauser, as PI of COBE/DIRBE, made the definitive absolute measurement in 1998, which required exceptionally careful modelling of zodiacal and Galactic foregrounds. The result was striking: the infrared background carries energy comparable to the optical one, so about half of all starlight ever emitted has been absorbed by dust and re-radiated. Optical surveys had therefore missed a large part of the universe's history. This finding motivated submillimetre surveys, Spitzer, Herschel and Planck, and it frames JWST's study of obscured galaxy growth. It is a fundamental measurement of the universe's energy budget, obtained through heroic calibration of space instruments.
